headline: Smartphone video and images yield person-specific mechanical and physiological phenotypes
label: Smartphone Individualized Physiological Phenotyping
summary: Low-cost smartphone capture is being paired with learned and physics-constrained models to produce individual-level biomechanical and health outputs.
synthesis: The dominant thread is individualized inference from smartphone-scale capture: a single video or image set is mapped to person-specific mechanical or physiological quantities. OpenCap Monocular estimates 3D skeletal kinematics and kinetics from one smartphone video using pose refinement, constrained skeletal modeling, and physics-based terms. A gait foundation model learns embeddings from 3D skeletal motion of 3,414 adults and predicts age, BMI, visceral fat, and other multi-system phenotypes. PhotoScan, pretrained on UK Biobank and fine-tuned on clinical cohorts, estimates body composition from smartphone images for cardiometabolic risk assessment. The three items differ in modality and endpoint, so the shared element is a workflow of learned or physics-constrained models operating on low-cost input to yield individual-level outputs. What is new is the pairing of smartphone-scale capture with such models, evaluated against mechanical or phenotypic targets.
